lines: NOTICE OF FUNDING AVAILABILITY (NOFA) FOR
AFFORDABLE MULTIFAMILY RENTAL HOUSING,
ROUND 33
QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS NO. 2
Issued November 23, 2026
Are rehabilitation applications/projects required to submit schematic design with all the
threshold requirements (title sheet, survey, site map, landscape plan, unit plans, sections,
etc.) or just the Rehabilitation only requirements (a PNA, schedule of va lues, conceptual
energy model, narrative)? Rehabilitation projects often do not commission full drawings
until after funding awards as they do not have to go through entitlement review and
approval.
All projects must provide threshold documentation, as identified to be elig ible for funding
consideration.
We have a project with NPLH and LACDA PBVs - are we still able to apply for additional
funding in NOFA 33 for a mix of SN and GA units?
Yes. Projects that only have NPLH funding are eligible for reapplication.
The Underwriting Guidelines note that GA projects need 3-month Operating Reserves, and
SN require 6 months. What is the requirement for mixed population projects?
If a project has Special Needs units, a six-month reserve is required.
For projects with 20% or more SN at 30% AMI, do we need an additional 10% of GA units
affordable at 30% AMI?
If the project is already reserving 20% of total units for a Special Needs population, the project
does not need to provide an additional 10% of units at 30% AMI.
We have Special Needs (SN) units at 1BR, and General Affordable (GA) from 0-2 BR. Is this
acceptable per 3.3.2 "Proposed projects must demonstrate that Special Needs units are
integrated with other units in the project and reflect the same unit types (numb er of
bedrooms)."
Special Needs units must be integrated throughout the development and not restricted to a
specific area separate from the General Affordable units.

November 23, 2026
Page 2
Does an REO need to be submitted for all project sponsors or only the one providing
experience?
REO schedules are required for all applicant sponsors.
For a proposed eight -story, 67 -unit affordable multifamily new -construction project
located in Culver City and seeking LACDA NOFA Round 33 funding, could LACDA please
confirm: 1. Whether California commercial prevailing-wage rates are required. 2. Whether
NOFA 33 funding independently requires compliance with a Project Labor Agreement
(PLA) or the Los Angeles County Community Workforce Agreement (CWA), and whether
any unit-count or construction-cost thresholds apply. 3. Whether there are additional local
or targeted hiring requirements associated with NOFA 33 funding. We would appreciate
clarification so that our construction cost estimates accurately reflect the applicable labor
requirements.
1. NOFA Section 7.11, Prevailing Wages, identifies prevailing wage requirements.
2. Depending on funding provided, location, and other requirements, a PLA or CWA may be
applicable. There is insufficient information provided regarding the entire scope of the
project to make a determination at this point.
3. NOFA Section 7.19, Local and Targeted Worker Hiring Program, identifies local hiring
requirements.
I own a 4,788-square-foot property at 3565 Wesley Street in Culver City and am exploring
an affordable multifamily housing development. Culver City's October 1, 2026 , planning
letter identifies 11 units of base development potential under SB 79, with the possibility of
up to 23 units through State Density Bonus Law, subject to affordability requirements and
physical feasibility. I understand that Round 33 requires at least 15 permanent rental units,
attendance at the October 28 mandatory proposers conference, and submission of a Real
Estate Owned Schedule by November 3. I would appreciate clarification of the following: If
an experienced affordable housing developer attended the October 28 conference and
submitted its qualifying REO Schedule on time, may that developer submit a new
application for my property, even though I was not involved in those earlier steps?
Yes, a developer that attended the Proposers Conference and meets qualifying criteria for the
REO can apply to develop the property.
Does the November 3 REO requirement apply to the developer's overall real estate
portfolio, rather than requiring my specific property to have been identified by November
3? If the developer previously submitted and qualified through an REO Schedule within
the preceding 12 months, would that satisfy the requirement?
NOFA 33 Questions & Answers No. 2
November 23, 2026
Page 3
Yes, the REO requirement applies to the applicant/developer’s overall real estate portfolio . The
requirement is satisfied if the developer qualified through a REO submittal within the preceding
12 months.
Could a privately owned Culver City property qualify for Round 33 capital funding through
an eligible joint venture or a long-term ground lease of at least 55 years? Would a proposed
15-to-23-unit project qualify for consideration if the final unit count, affordability
restrictions, and financing are established before application submission? Are there any
additional readiness or site -control requirements that would prevent a newly formed
partnership from applying by December 3, 2026?
Yes, a privately owned Culver City property can qualify for Round 33 capital funding through an
eligible joint venture with a qualified developer. A proposed 15 -23 unit project could qualify for
consideration if the final unit count, affordability restrictions, and financing are established before
application submittal and meet all NOFA guidelines. Refer to the NOFA Guidelines and Checklist
for more information when considering project readiness for application submittal.
In the project information section, you are required to select a TCAC housing type for tax
credit projects. If our 4% project will be “untargeted” housing type (permitted under
CDLAC/TCAC for 4% projects), which TCAC housing type should we select in this section?
Identification of a housing type for LACDA funding is required. Select the type that closest reflects
the project.
If the entity satisfying the supportive-housing experience requirements under Section 5.2.2
serves as the project’s Managing General Partner, may the applicant rely on that entity’s
experience for PBV eligibility? Must that entity hold any minimum ownershi p interest or
controlling interest in the project partnership or general partner entity, including a 51%
interest, or serve as a Lead or Joint Developer?
The entity satisfying supportive housing experience must be the lead developer, as defined in the
NOFA.
Please confirm that a Request for Compliance is no longer required.
Correct.
Rosie's Touch is seeking an experienced affordable housing development partner. Since
we did not attend the mandatory Proposers' Conference, can we participate in Round 33
with a development partner who attended? Would that partner need to be the lead
applicant?
NOFA 33 Questions & Answers No. 2
November 23, 2026
Page 4
Yes. A less experienced applicant may partner with an eligible applicant. Please note that the
NOFA states, “Any joint partnership between a developer, a lead developer, and/or managing
general partner must be formed prior to the application deadline. Limited partnership does not
have to be formed prior to the application deadline, but the applicant must submit documentation
detailing each entity’s role and responsibilities.”
"Based on LACDA guidelines, please confirm if an applicant is applying for PBVs that they
can only apply for capital funding for SN units", and the LACDA response was "No". Can
you please confirm than if an applicant applies for PBVs, that applicant can also apply for
both capital funding for SN and GA units all in the same application?
Applicants can apply for both capital funding for SN and GA units in the same application. Section
3.3 Eligible Projects and General Requirements indicates that applicants may request: 1. Funding
and PBVs for eligible Special Needs units; 2. Funding for Spe cial Needs units only; 3. Funding
for General Affordable units only; 4. Funding for both Special Needs and General Affordable units.
General Affordable units are not eligible for PBVs. Projects requesting funding for Special Needs
units are eligible for capital funding and PBVs, or capital only. Only applicants meeting Supportive
Housing Developers and PBV Eligibility criteria (see NOFA Section 5.2.2) are eligible to receive
both capital and Project-Based rental assistance.
Under Section 5.2.5, when an experienced architect joins another firm as a full -time
employee and principal, can their qualifying projects completed as Architect of Record at
a prior practice satisfy the individual architect experience requirement and coun t toward
the current firm’s experience score, and, if so, what role must that individual hold on the
proposed project and what supporting documentation is required?
Yes, the employee , who joined the firm as a full -time employee and principal, can use thei r
previously completed qualifying projects as Architect of Record to satisfy the architect experience
requirement and obtain experience points . The employee/principal must be the Architect of
Record for the proposed project. The Project Information Workbook has the Architect Experience
tab where the information can be provided. The architect’s resume can also be submitted.
Under Section 3.7.3, what minimum expiration date should an Exclusive Negotiating
Agreement with a public agency have to satisfy the requirement that site control extend
through the expected award timeline for NOFA 33?
The minimum expiration date for the Exclusive Negotiating Agreement should extend through the
expected timeline for award of NOFA funds – at least through April 2027.
The appraisal requirements state that the appraisal "must be conducted prior to or within
30 days of executing a purchase contract". This contradicts the checklist's language of
180 days. Can you confirm what's the right number?
NOFA 33 Questions & Answers No. 2
November 23, 2026
Page 5
The appraisal must be conducted prior to or within 30 days of executing a purch ase contract.
Appraisals are valid for 180 days.
NOFA 33 Section 3.3.2 "MINIMUM PROJECT REQUIREMENTS" states that "Transportation,
services, and other amenities are within a 1/3 -mile diameter of the site." Is this accurate
and is there a list of amenities required with corresponding distances?
Yes, the 1/3 -mile diameter as stated in the NOFA is correct. Amenities are publicly available
services and facilities that improve quality of life for project residents, examples of which include
grocery stores, schools, medical clinics, pharmacies, parks, and community centers.
